newsitem.title: USA: Columbia Labs says FDA approves Crinone.
newsitem.headline: Columbia Labs says FDA approves Crinone.

text.p: Columbia Laboratories Inc. Wednesday said it has received U.S. marketing approval for Crinone from the Food and Drug Administration.
Columbia said the product will be marketed by the Wyeth-Ayerst division of American Home Products Corp.
The drug was approved for use as a progesterone supplement or replacement as part of an Assisted Reproductive Technology treatment for infertile women with progesterone deficiency.
Crinone is a vaginally delivered natural progesterone gel. Assisted Reproductive procedures include in-vitro fertilization, ovum donation and stimulated cycles.

A second new drug application for Crinone's use in patients with secondary amenorrhea, or loss of menstrual period, and hormonal imbalance is currently being reviewed by the FDA and approval is expected in the third quarter, the company said..
Columbia's said that through it patented Bioadhesive Delivery System, Crinone is the first product to deliver progesterone directly to the uterus, thereby maximizing therapeutic benefits.
